chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with potassium permanganate, chlorates, carbides, picrates, water.
chemicals.storage_temp: Polyethylene acid cabinet with secondary sump
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, bases, organic materials, chlorates, metals
chemicals.sds_key_points: #1 industrial chemical by volume. Chars wood and paper on contact.

chemicals.name: Sulfuric Acid, Spent or Battery Fluid Acid
chemicals.color: Dark cloudy or black acidic liquid
chemicals.ppe_level: Acid apron, face shield, neoprene gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Severe acid burns, blindness; spent acid contains dissolved heavy metals (lead, arsenic).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush 20+ minutes with water.
chemicals.antidote: Water irrigation; neutralize spill with soda ash.
chemicals.fire_response: Do not add water directly to concentrated acid.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with bases, cyanides, sulfides, and organics.
chemicals.storage_temp: Polyethylene acid drum
chemicals.sds_key_points: HazMat recycling & warehouse pallet spill staple.

chemicals.name: Tars, Liquid, Including Road Asphalt and Cutback Bitumen
chemicals.odor: Tarry petroleum + rotten-egg H2S headspace odor
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA (tank headspace accumulates lethal Hydrogen Sulfide H2S gas!)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe full-thickness thermal burns from adhering 180C bitumen; lethal H2S knockdown in tanker headspace!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. COOL HOT ASPHALT ON SKIN WITH COLD WATER FOR 20+ MIN—DO NOT PEEL OFF ADHERED ASPHALT! (Use mineral oil, baby oil, or Polysporin ointment later at hospital to dissolve gently).
chemicals.antidote: Cold water cooling in place; mineral oil / petrolatum dissolution.
chemicals.fire_response: DO NOT spray solid water stream into hot molten asphalt tank (1:1,700 steam expansion causes violent boilover eruption)! Use foam or fine water fog lightly.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes on contact with Liquid Oxygen (LOX)!
chemicals.storage_temp: Insulated heated tank with H2S vent warning
chemicals.sds_key_points: Two critical rules: (1) Never peel cooled asphalt off burned skin, and (2) Never shoot water into a hot asphalt tanker (steam boilover)!

chemicals.name: Toluene (Methylbenzene)
chemicals.ppe_level: Viton or PVA gloves + splash goggles
chemicals.symptoms: Headache, ataxia, hallucinations, CNS depression, cardiac arrhythmia, renal tubular acidosis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes/skin. 3. Do NOT induce vomiting (aspiration hazard).
chemicals.fire_response: Flammable liquid (flash point 4C). Static electricity during pouring can ignite vapor! Always bond and ground drums.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts with nitric/sulfuric acid to form explosive TNT intermediates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Nitric acid, strong oxidizers, dinitrogen tetroxide
chemicals.sds_key_points: Core solvent in auto body shops, lacquer thinners, and contact cements. Static spark hazard!

chemicals.name: VX Nerve Agent
chemicals.synonyms: O-ethyl S-[2-(diisopropylamino)ethyl] methylphosphonothioate, Persistent Nerve Agent
chemicals.color: Amber, odorless oily liquid (very slow evaporation)
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A CBRN Vapor-Tight Suit + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Single drop (10 mg) on skin is fatal! Local sweating & fasciculations at drop site, followed by SLUDGEM, miosis, status epilepticus, and respiratory arrest.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Immediate RSDL (Reactive Skin Decontamination Lotion) or 0.5% bleach blot. 2. 3x DuoDote / ATNAA auto-injectors (Atropine 6 mg + 2-PAM 1800 mg) + Diazepam/Midazolam.
chemicals.antidote: Atropine + Pralidoxime (2-PAM) + Midazolam + RSDL skin decon.
chemicals.fire_response: CBRN Military EOD required.
chemicals.reactivity: Persistent contact hazard for weeks on surfaces unless oxidized with bleach/RSDL.
chemicals.storage_temp: Military CBRN containment only
chemicals.sds_key_points: Most potent persistent nerve agent; acts primarily as a contact poison on skin/gear.

chemicals.name: Vinyl Chloride, Stabilized
chemicals.odor: Faint sweet pleasant odor at high concentrations
chemicals.symptoms: CNS narcosis, dizziness, frostbite, angiosarcoma of the liver; combustion releases massive HCl and Phosgene clouds!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind. 2. Oxygen. 3. Warm frostbite.
chemicals.fire_response: Rail tank car derailment hazard (East Palestine profile). Burns with heavy black soot releasing Hydrogen Chloride and Phosgene. Evacuate 1 mile if tank is in fire.
chemicals.reactivity: Polymerizes violently in heat/sunlight or with peroxides.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool stabilized pressure vessel

reactivity_rules.consequence: CATASTROPHIC MIXING HAZARD: Releases lethal Chloramine vapor immediately. Causes severe chemical pneumonitis, pulmonary edema, and asphyxiation.
CATASTROPHIC MIXING HAZARD: Acid protonates hypochlorite to liberate dense greenish-yellow Chlorine gas (IDLH 10 ppm). Rapid respiratory arrest.
EXTREME LETHALITY: Acids convert cyanide salts into volatile Hydrogen Cyanide gas (IDLH 50 ppm). Knockdown and cellular asphyxiation within seconds. Prepare Cyanokit (Hydroxocobalamin).
LETHAL GAS EVOLUTION: Releases rotten-egg H2S gas that paralyzes olfactory nerves above 100 ppm and causes instant knockdown + flammable vapor cloud.
VIOLENT HYDROLYSIS: Generates explosive flammable gas and extreme heat sufficient to auto-ignite. DO NOT USE WATER—use Class D dry powder or dry sand.
RUNAWAY EXOTHERMIC NITRATION: Concentrated nitric acid + organic solvents/fuels causes spontaneous ignition, dense red-brown NO2 cloud, and vessel rupture.
HYPERGOLIC / RAPID OXIDATION: Oxidizer supplies oxygen directly to fuel, causing violent flash fire or detonation even without external air.
EXPLOSION & TOXIC VAPOR: Strong oxidizers (chlorine, hypochlorites, peroxides, chromates) react with ammonia to form shock-sensitive explosive compounds.
EXTREME HEAT EVOLUTION: Rapid neutralization boils liquid instantly, violently ejecting concentrated acid/alkali droplets.
EXPLOSIVE REACTION: Alkali metals (Sodium, Lithium, Potassium) detonate on contact with halogens or halogenated solvents (Brake Cleaner/Perc).
CRITICAL WORKSHOP HAZARD: Chlorinated brake cleaner (Tetrachloroethylene) reacts explosively with sodium/aluminum/magnesium shavings or converts to deadly Phosgene gas in welding arcs.
CATALYTIC RUNAWAY: Transition metals (iron, copper, rust, brass) catalyze violent decomposition of concentrated Hydrogen Peroxide or Organic Peroxides.
EV / WAREHOUSE RUNAWAY: Breached cells react with acid or salt water to vent white vapor containing lethal Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) and explosive H2.
EXPLOSIVE ACETYLIDE: Acetylene forms friction-sensitive explosive acetylides with copper/brass (>65% Cu), silver, or mercury, and explodes on contact with chlorine.
MASS EXPLOSION HAZARD: Ammonium nitrate sensitized by hydrocarbons (diesel/oil >0.2%) or chlorates transitions from deflagration to high-order detonation.
CORROSIVE DISSOLUTION: Dissolves glass/silica (forming toxic SiF4 gas) and reacts with metals to build explosive hydrogen pressure in sealed drums.
AUTOCATALYTIC RUNAWAY: Trace acid, base, or iron oxide rust triggers violent exothermic polymerization in storage tanks, leading to catastrophic BLEVE.
DRUM RUPTURE HAZARD: Water or amines react with isocyanates/monomers to generate rapid CO2 gas pressure and heat, rupturing sealed containers.
